compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The operator's macOS host accumulates `rebar-opcert-*` directories in the system temp dir (`tempfile.gettempdir()`), each holding an `opcert-key` private-key copy: 621 on 2026-10-31, roughly 140-200 new per day since 2026-10-28. `rebar.opcert_service.keyprov.compose_signer` creates that shape (`tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rebar-opcert-")` + `opcert-key`), and only `OpcertSigner.cleanup()` removes it. Private-key copies left in a shared temp dir widen key exposure and grow without bound.

Measured cause (evidence in a ticket comment): running each signer-composing test module alone with `TMPDIR` pointed at an empty sandbox leaves 8 dirs from `tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py` and 1 from `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity_heldout.py`; the other 5 signer modules leave 0. Those 2 modules pass `signer=_signer(tmp_path)` inline to `run_job` and never call `cleanup()`. 4 of the 9 sandbox dirs also hold `opcert-key.pub` (written by signing), the same 44% ratio seen on the host (276 of 621). No process on the host has any of these files open, and no `rebar-mcp` process runs on the host.

A second, smaller gap: `compose_signer` removes its runtime dir only when `OpcertKeyError` is raised. Any other exception after `mkdtemp` (an `OSError` from writing the copy, or `KeyboardInterrupt`/`SystemExit` while `ssh-keygen` validates it) leaves the dir and key copy behind.

## Approach
Keep the existing ownership model (the signer's owner calls `cleanup()`, as the module docstring states) and make every owner honour it:
1. In `tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py` and `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity_heldout.py`, replace the bare `_signer(tmp_path)` helper with a pytest fixture that composes the signer, yields it, and calls `cleanup()` in teardown. Tests that call `cleanup()` themselves keep doing so (it is idempotent: `rmtree(ignore_errors=True)`).
2. In `compose_signer`, widen the cleanup handler from `except OpcertKeyError` to `except BaseException`, re-raising unchanged, so no exception or interrupt between `mkdtemp` and the return leaves a key copy.

No production signing behaviour changes: the copy is still made once at startup and removed by its owner. The MCP server's `main()` already removes the copy in a `finally` after `run_mcp` drains on SIGTERM (commit 1c51c9dcd06). SIGKILL cannot be intercepted by any in-process cleanup and is out of scope.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/opcert_service/keyprov.py` — `compose_signer` cleans its runtime dir on any exception.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py` — signer fixture with teardown cleanup replaces inline `_signer(tmp_path)` calls.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity_heldout.py` — same fixture change.
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py` (new) — regression tests below.

Non-goals: removing the existing leaked copies through code (a one-time manual cleanup after the fix lands, recorded on this ticket); changing where or whether the key is copied.

## Testing
New `tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py`:
- Suite-level regression: run `tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py` and `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity_heldout.py` in a nested pytest (`tests/_nested_pytest.run_nested_pytest`) with `TMPDIR` set to an empty sandbox; assert the child passes and the sandbox holds 0 `rebar-opcert-*` entries. Before the fix this finds 9.
- Error path: with `tempfile.tempdir` pointed at an empty sandbox, make writing the key copy raise `OSError`, and separately make key validation raise `KeyboardInterrupt`; assert the exception propagates unchanged and the sandbox holds 0 `rebar-opcert-*` entries. Before the fix both leave 1.
- Happy path: a valid key composes a signer whose copy exists until `cleanup()`, after which the sandbox is empty.
Then run the 7 signer-related unit modules (`test_opcert_service*.py`, `test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup.py`, `test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py`, `test_mcp_drain_signing_iguanodon.py`, `test_opcert_privkey_env_pop_932d.py`) with a sandboxed `TMPDIR` and confirm all pass with 0 leftover dirs, plus `make lint` and `make typecheck`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The leaking caller(s) are identified by a before/after count, recorded in a ticket comment.
- [x] Running the signer-composing unit test modules leaves no new `rebar-opcert-*` directory in the system temp dir, enforced by a regression test that fails before the fix.
- [x] `compose_signer` leaves no `rebar-opcert-*` directory when any exception, including `KeyboardInterrupt`, is raised after the directory is created, enforced by a regression test.
- [x] The existing leaked copies are removed by a one-time manual operator cleanup (not by rebar code) after the fix lands, with before/after counts recorded in a ticket comment.
